final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position by conceding the same core defects identified in the initial report. That reframing is useful but not curative. A caveated certification posture can be descriptively more careful than an overbroad compliance claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely disclosure in the writeup or monitoring language; it is an unfulfilled policy condition. On the available record, the affected enterprise refund workflow remains tied to a named launch use case or customer commitment, legal review is still open, and there is no evidence of either required disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. Under the stated policy text, those missing predicates keep certification from being evidentially supported as compliant.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required launch disclosure for the enterprise refund workflow limitation was made before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case before launch.
Legal review on disclosure remains unresolved, and the record does not contain a final legal determination.
The policy text states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the packet indicates this segment is named in a renewal success plan.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents remain secondary considerations and do not satisfy the policy predicate for a material named use-case limitation.
